silica.source: Kitamura et al. (2007) 0.1-20 um stitched with Popova et al. (1972) 7-50 um at 20 um (Lederer 2026 set); Franta et al. (2016) as the alternative
silica.temperature: room temperature (refractiveindex.info headers: Kitamura 'near room temperature', Popova/Franta 'room temperature')
silica.interpolation: linear in wavelength, n and k separately (scipy interp1d; saimon.materials.SilicaRefractiveIndex)
silica.extrapolation: linear extrapolation beyond the table ends (fill_value='extrapolate'); never exercised: the table covers 0.1-50 um
silica.density_source: saimon.sai.SILICA_DENSITY_KG_M3 = 2200 (amorphous silica; code constant, no citation in the code)

LM65T223.note: linear interpolation in wavelength; used only 2.05-26 um; below 2.05 um Palmer-Williams (300 K) + Lorentz-Lorenz to 215 K

LM72T213.note: linear interpolation in wavelength; used only 2.05-26 um; below 2.05 um Palmer-Williams (300 K) + Lorentz-Lorenz to 215 K

B70T215.note: linear interpolation in wavelength; used only 2.05-26 um; below 2.05 um Palmer-Williams (300 K) + Lorentz-Lorenz to 215 K

sulfuric_acid.visible: Palmer & Williams (1975) 300 K tables (data/optics/palmer_williams_75_combined_300K.csv), Lorentz-Lorenz corrected to 215 K (saimon.sulfate_background.sulfuric_acid_at_temperature), 0.30-2.04 um
sulfuric_acid.temperature: Lund Myhre 65 wt% at 223 K (quiet calibration), 72 wt% at 213 K (post-HT bracket), Biermann 70 wt% at 215 K (optics-swap bracket)
sulfuric_acid.interpolation: linear in wavelength (np.interp on the wavenumber-ordered table), n and k separately; k clipped >= 0
sulfuric_acid.extrapolation: TabulatedRI holds the end values beyond 26 um (tables used only 2.05-26 um); far-IR calcite row (26-31 um) extrapolates
sulfuric_acid.density: H2SO4 density from the Myhre (1998) polynomial for the Lorentz-Lorenz correction; droplet density ~1700 kg m^-3 in the number-density conversions

calcite.interpolation: linear in wavelength, n and k separately, on the ray tables (saimon.materials.RayMeanUniaxialRefractiveIndex)
calcite.extrapolation: end values held (clamped) beyond the table ends
calcite.temperature: room-temperature laboratory reflectance tabulations (no low-temperature tables exist)
calcite.source: Long et al. (1993) Lorentz-oscillator fits (o and e rays) evaluated 0.1-1000 um on a 20000-point log grid (the Stardust calcite optical set, Lederer 2026 convention); visible n from the oscillator model

handbook_visible_indices_for_reference.note: Handbook of Mineralogy calcite Na-D; NOT what the file holds (see n_at_0p5893um)

dolomite.interpolation: linear in wavelength, n and k separately, on the ray tables (saimon.materials.RayMeanUniaxialRefractiveIndex)
dolomite.extrapolation: end values held (clamped) beyond the table ends
dolomite.temperature: room-temperature laboratory reflectance tabulations (no low-temperature tables exist)
dolomite.source: Querry (1987, CRDEC-CR-88009) o/e tables via refractiveindex.info (data/optics/Dolomite_Querry-{o,e}.yml), 2.5-40 (o) / 2.5-50 um (e); reproduce/convert_querry_optics.py: k clamped >= 0, flat visible/NIR anchors at the Handbook-of-Mineralogy Na-D indices (n_o = 1.679, n_e = 1.500, k = 0) at 0.20, 0.5893, 0.6563 um, linear bridge 0.6563-2.5 um
dolomite.density_source: saimon.sai.DOLOMITE_DENSITY_KG_M3 = 2860 (Handbook of Mineralogy, D(meas.) = 2.86 g/cm^3; code comment)

alumina.interpolation: linear in wavelength, n and k separately, on the ray tables (saimon.materials.RayMeanUniaxialRefractiveIndex)
alumina.extrapolation: end values held (clamped) beyond the table ends
alumina.temperature: room-temperature laboratory reflectance tabulations (no low-temperature tables exist)
alumina.source: Querry (1985, CRDC-CR-85034) sapphire o/e tables via refractiveindex.info (data/optics/Al2O3_Querry-{o,e}.yml), 0.21-55.6 um; reproduce/convert_querry_optics.py: k clamped >= 0 and set to zero below 6 um; ray-mean n below 5 um replaced by a Cauchy fit

conventions.b: Clausius-Mossotti inversion of the mean Rayleigh polarizability (2 o + 1 e)/3 -> Mie (Rayleigh-exact)
conventions.c: cross-section average (2 Q_o + Q_e)/3 of Mie with m_o and with m_e
